subject: Private upgrade runway — shepherding schedule, pin release and rollback authority
messages:
From: Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Hi Hannah and team,

We're preparing for a quarterly maintenance window for our private deployment (VPC) and want to align with Redwood's upgrade cadence. Our infra folks flagged the next available downtime on the evening of Sept 9 (UTC). Primary asks:
- Can Redwood shepherd a minor service-side patch to the private control plane (rolling restart of agents + pinned model versions)?
- We need explicit rollback criteria and an authorization path in case business SLA is impacted.
- Acme requires artifact-level evidence (pre/post telemetry) for audit.

I've attached a checklist of our internal preflight items. Please confirm who on Redwood's side will own the run and what the communication cadence will be (bridge, slack channel).

Thanks,
Rick
SRE Lead, Acme Financial
[Attachment: acme-maintenance-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Hi Rick — thanks for the checklist. We can own the patch window on Sept 9 evening (UTC) but want to propose a short dry‑run the week prior (Sept 6) for the canary group. High level plan below; I want Karthik and Neha to confirm the technical and compliance gates.

Planned sequence (high level):
1) Preflight (Sept 6 dry run): simulate staged cutover in a non-production mirror; confirm KV cache warmup and model pin compatibility.
2) Canary (Sept 9 19:00 UTC): 5% traffic to pinned variant on single rack; monitor latency P95 and error rate for 30m.
3) Ramp (Sept 9 19:45 UTC): 25% -> 60% traffic slices with automated batching thresholds.
4) Full cutover (Sept 9 21:00 UTC): complete rollout if no gating alerts.

Rollbacks: immediate rollback to previous pinned tag if any of the gating rules fire (see Karthik's note) — we will keep a short rollback window (first 45 minutes after canary start) where we prioritize availability over throughput.

Communication: dedicated bridge (Zoom), #acme-maintenance Slack channel, and real‑time telemetry to your SRE. We'll produce an artifacts bundle (pre/post traces, token-level cost delta, and version tags).

Karthik / Neha — can you confirm the rollback criteria granularity (latency, synthetic failures, KV-miss slope) and whether we need an explicit exec-level approval for full cutover?

- Hannah
Director, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Heads up on the technical gating we'll enforce: listed as absolute abort triggers unless explicitly overridden by execs.

Abort triggers (immediate rollback):
- P95 token latency increase > 35% over baseline for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Error rate (5xx or model-serving grpc failures) > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes.
- KV cache miss rate rising > 3x baseline leading to increased cold-token CPU.
- Model output regression detected by our smoke prompts (quality failure).

Soft gates (operator review):
- Token cost delta > 20% across the canary window.
- Elevated tail latency for non-peak but not sustained.

Operational notes:
- We'll pin the control-plane microservice to the git tag release/v2.3.1-acme and keep the previous tag available as release/v2.3.0-acme.
- Network: expect a short BGP refresh on the router pair during drain; Connor will validate routing preflight and confirm netops blackout windows.
- Rollback mechanics: automated routing policy reverts to previous model variant plus an immediate KV cache flush and rehydrate window (approx 12–15 minutes to warm).

I attached the rollback decision doc with specific observability queries and playbook steps.

- Karthik
Principal IR Engineer
[Attachment: rollback-criteria.md (text/markdown)]

From: ops@edgenet.io <ops@edgenet.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Sep 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Thanks team — EdgeNet here. A couple of network-level asks:
- Please confirm the exact time we should place the maintenance BGP community to avoid unintended route flaps (we prefer 19:00:30 UTC; sticky time helps automation).
- We'll publish a pre-cutover netops bulletin and need the exact IPs of the canary hosts so our ACL automation can whitelist them during the test.

We also attached our runbook dry‑run results from Aug 29 (sanity pass). No issues found but note an observed TCP queue spike on host node-12 during the dry run.

- EdgeNet Support
[Attachment: runbook-dryrun-results-20280829.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>, Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Sep 2028 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Agree with Karthik's gates. A few compliance bullets I want documented and signed off before full cutover:
- Evidence package: pre/post traces, audit logs (KMS access events), and a token‑level cost report.
- Retention: Acme asked that the audit artifacts be retained for 90 days in their S3; we will produce and push a signed tarball to the provided bucket.
- Exec approval: For a rollback that extends beyond the 45 minute 'safety window' we require an ops exec to sign off (Naomi Feldman will be available).

Connor — please confirm the verification steps for KV rehydration and the expected warmup time you measured during the dry run. Connor, please also post the canary host IP list into #acme-maintenance by EOD Friday.

- Neha
Head of Customer Compliance

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rick Bailey <rick.bailey@acmefin.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private maintenance window request — proposed Sept window

Final confirmation and ownership:

1) Dates & times
- Dry run: Sept 6 18:30 UTC (mirror / no client traffic) — complete.
- Canary start: Sept 9 19:00:30 UTC (5% traffic) — EdgeNet requested exact second latch.
- Ramp windows and full cutover: as previously detailed.

2) Rollback authority
- Immediate rollback action is owned by on-call deployment lead (Karthik) when abort triggers occur.
- If rollback extends longer than 45 minutes or requires emergency unpinning we will escalate to Naomi Feldman for exec approval. Naomi: please provide a single-line approve/reject checklist in this thread so we have a written trail.

3) Deliverables post-window
- Artifacts tarball uploaded to Acme S3 (90‑day retention).
- Runbook postmortem and smoke-prompt scorecard within 48 hours.

4) Bridge & comms
- Zoom bridge will be created and shared 24 hours in advance.
- Slack channel: #acme-maintenance (we'll invite EdgeNet ops).

Connor / EdgeNet — please share the canary host IP list to the slack channel; Karthik will publish the exact observability queries we use for gating.

Thanks everyone — I will trigger the calendar invites and publish the doc link to the runbook.

- Hannah
Director, Deployments
Redwood Inference
